content_units: Auckland Commuter Car Verdict
For   18,000 km/year  , a   NZ$16,000 cap  , and a goal of   low running costs + solid 4-year reliability  , the strongest first shortlist is:
1.   Option C — 2015 Honda Fit Hybrid
2.   Option A — 2016 Toyota Corolla
3.   Option B — 2017 Mazda3

The Fit Hybrid is the cheapest to run day to day if the battery system is healthy. The Corolla is the safest low-risk ownership pick overall. The Mazda3 is still a good car, but for this brief it is slightly weaker on fuel cost and resale certainty.
Used Car Comparison Table
Option   Price   Odometer   Running Costs   Maintenance Considerations   Resale Outlook   Best Fit
A. 2016 Toyota Corolla       NZ$15,800       92,000 km     Low   Routine servicing; CVT/fluid history worth checking; generally simple and proven   Strong   Best all-round low-risk choice

B. 2017 Mazda3       NZ$14,900       108,000 km     Moderate   Higher km; check suspension wear, tyres, brakes, transmission service history   Good, but not as strong as Corolla   Best if driving feel matters more

C. 2015 Honda Fit Hybrid       NZ$15,200       88,000 km     Very low   Hybrid battery and transmission system health are key; must verify service history   Good if condition is strong   Best for lowest fuel spend
4-Year Ownership Tradeoffs
Option A: 2016 Toyota Corolla
-   Reliability:   Very strong reputation, especially for commuter use.
-   Maintenance:   Usually predictable—oil, filters, brakes, tyres, fluids. Lower chance of surprise repair bills than the other two.
-   Fuel economy:   Good, but usually not as cheap to fuel as the Fit Hybrid.
-   Resale:   Likely the strongest of the three in NZ because Corollas are easy to sell and trusted by buyers.
-   Main caution:   Confirm whether it is a NZ-new or import example and check full servicing, especially transmission/CVT care if applicable.
Option B: 2017 Mazda3
-   Reliability:   Generally good, but this one starts with the   highest km  .

-   Maintenance:   Expect normal servicing plus a greater chance of wear items sooner over your 4-year hold—suspension bushings, tyres, brakes, battery, and possibly more frequent attention as it moves well past 150,000 km.
-   Fuel economy:   Usually decent, but weaker than the Fit Hybrid and often a little worse than a small-efficient Corolla setup for pure commuting cost.
-   Resale:   Reasonable, though a higher-km Mazda3 after 4 more years may be less appealing than an equivalent Corolla.
-   Main caution:   At your usage, this car could end up around   180,000 km   in 4 years, which pushes it deeper into higher-maintenance territory.
Option C: 2015 Honda Fit Hybrid
-   Reliability:   Can be very good, but hybrid condition matters more than with the other two.
-   Maintenance:   Routine costs can be low, but the ownership risk is concentrated in   hybrid battery health  , cooling components, and transmission/hybrid system behavior.
-   Fuel economy:   Best of the three for Auckland commuting, especially stop-start traffic.
-   Resale:   Small efficient hybrids stay attractive, though buyer confidence depends heavily on battery health and documentation.
-   Main caution:   A pre-purchase inspection should specifically assess hybrid system operation, warning lights, battery condition behavior, and service records.
What Matters Most for Your Use Case
With   72,000 km   of driving over 4 years, fuel spend will noticeably separate these cars.
-   Fit Hybrid:   likely lowest fuel bill overall
-   Corolla:   likely slightly higher fuel spend, but lower mechanical uncertainty
-   Mazda3:   likely highest fuel cost of the three, plus highest wear-and-tear exposure due to starting mileage
So the decision is really:
-   Lowest running cost winner:   Honda Fit Hybrid
-   Lowest ownership-risk winner:   Toyota Corolla
First Shortlist Recommendation
1) First shortlist: 2015 Honda Fit Hybrid

If inspection and service history are strong, this is the best match for your stated priority of   low running costs  . Over 18,000 km/year, the fuel savings can be meaningful, and its odometer is also the lowest after the Corolla-adjacent range.
2) Safer alternative: 2016 Toyota Corolla

If you want the car with the best chance of being boring, dependable, and easy to resell in 4 years, pick this instead. It is the most balanced choice and the one I would recommend if you are slightly risk-averse.
3) Third choice: 2017 Mazda3
Only shortlist first if you strongly prefer how it drives or its features/comfort. For your priorities, it is not the optimal value-over-4-years pick.
Purchase Filters Before You Commit
-   Fit Hybrid:   insist on a hybrid-aware inspection and battery/system check
-   Corolla:   confirm transmission service history, accident history, and whether it has full documented maintenance
-   Mazda3:   inspect suspension, tyres, brakes, and signs of deferred maintenance due to higher km
